$comment: The 40-point human half of ratings/RUBRIC.md. Every sub-score carries a justification naming specific content; the scorer REFUSES any entry whose `why` is shorter than 15 characters. Scored 13 Aug 2026. Disagree with a number? The justification is right there — argue with that.

failureModes.asks: Does it document what goes wrong, with the symptom you'd actually observe first?

reuseLeverage.asks: How much time does it save, on how many future tasks?

maintenance.asks: INVERTED RISK. 10 = principles that won't age. 0 = wrong within months.

failureModes.why: Nine numbered gotchas, each symptom-first: the four-build login saga with the exact 'nothing happens and no error' signature, the domain move that took the site down 20 minutes, 'day' being a reserved word shipping a 502, and the preview pane's specific lies.

reuseLeverage.why: Total leverage on its own project — a cold session can act from it — but essentially zero transfer to any other codebase. Depth is the value here, not breadth.

maintenance.why: 1,150 lines of live state: env inventories, cache-buster version numbers, per-area status tables. It dates its claims, which helps, but it decays weekly and needs deliberate upkeep.

failureModes.why: Strong on the honest-gaps side — mock extraction, throwaway /tmp SQLite, rules never tuned on a real L/C, no independent audit of money-critical logic — but lighter on operational symptom-to-cause traps than the site skills.

reuseLeverage.why: Carries the whole product thesis and the 18-rule engine, so a new session can continue the business as well as the code. Project-bound, but that project is a company.

maintenance.why: The strategy and the rule table are durable; the capability/gap list is a snapshot that goes stale the moment real extraction lands.

failureModes.why: Seven named traps that each cost real hours: .cmd argv truncation, the 7-day OAuth refresh-token death, Meta renaming metrics, Pillow without raqm, env-var newlines, the pre-parsed body that silently re-ran every sync, and @vercel/blob v1 rejecting private stores.

reuseLeverage.why: Runs an active system daily and most of its traps generalise to any scheduled agent on Windows talking to platform APIs.

maintenance.why: Built on three platform APIs that change without notice — the skill itself says Meta renames metrics constantly, which is an admission that parts of it will be wrong soon.

failureModes.why: The vanishing-logins diagnosis is exemplary and the 'never reintroduce fs writes in a handler' rule is stated as a standing prohibition, but fewer distinct failure signatures are catalogued than in the vishal-site skill.

reuseLeverage.why: Complete working guide for a live site including the deliberate page-split reasoning, but bounded to that codebase.

maintenance.why: Architecture notes are stable; the feature inventory and TODO list drift with every deploy.

failureModes.why: Built around the two failures that break almost every file-based Node app on Vercel — static assets 404ing because sendFile targets aren't bundled, and JSON writes vanishing on an ephemeral filesystem — with a stated diagnosis for each.

reuseLeverage.why: Applies to essentially any Express-shaped app deployed to serverless, and it ships an eval set and a store-adapter template, so it is reusable as code and not only as prose.

maintenance.why: Vercel's build behaviour is the substrate; includeFiles semantics and CLI flags have changed before and will again.

failureModes.why: Its whole thesis is that reported symptoms are unreliable and only measurement is not, and it ships three probe scripts rather than describing them.

reuseLeverage.why: Every project here has hit 'looks broken on my phone' at least once; the probes turn a vague complaint into pixel numbers on any site, framework or not.

maintenance.why: getBoundingClientRect and IntersectionObserver are stable web platform; only the preview-pane-specific notes are environment-bound.

failureModes.why: Covers the blank-canvas-in-preview problem and reduced-motion/off-screen pausing, but is more recipe than failure catalogue.

reuseLeverage.why: Narrow: it applies when a plain HTML/CSS/JS site needs an animated hero or a page split. Useful when it fires, rarely fires.

maintenance.why: Canvas 2D and DPR handling are stable; the preview-pane workaround is tied to one tool's current behaviour.

failureModes.why: Names the deploy failures that masquerade as a broken site — 401 deployment protection, framework:null producing a 404, a stray GitHub auto-connect — which is exactly the class that wastes hours.

reuseLeverage.why: Complete pipeline with four reference files, but only pays off when building that specific Next.js + R3F + motion + Lenis stack.

maintenance.why: Pinned to a fast-moving stack — Next App Router, Tailwind v4, react-three-fiber, drei, Framer Motion. Written 19 June 2026 and already at risk; this is the highest decay rate in the library.

failureModes.why: Almost none documented. It is a build recipe with a decision fork at the top, not a record of what went wrong.

reuseLeverage.why: Genuinely useful for the recurring 'personal brand site with an owner-editable panel' ask, and the two-stack fork is a real decision, but it duplicates material now better covered by newer skills.

maintenance.why: Stack-agnostic enough to age slowly, but the Bkash and booking sections are superseded by bkash-payment-integration and the vishal-agarwal-site consultation work.

failureModes.why: Built entirely around the real recurring failure — installed at local scope, works in one folder, invisible everywhere else — plus the three distinct reasons a skill doesn't appear in / and a stop-at-first-failure diagnostic ladder.

reuseLeverage.why: This exact task recurred more than fifteen times across the session history and had no skill covering it; it fires on every new MCP, skill or plugin.

maintenance.why: The scoping principle is durable but the CLI surface it depends on — flag names, settings.json keys, marketplace format — is young and changes.

failureModes.why: Names the real failure modes of the practice itself — producing a summary instead of an actionable skill, appending until it becomes a diary, and losing everything by writing it after the budget runs out — but it is a method, so there are fewer observable symptoms to catalogue.

reuseLeverage.why: The highest-leverage entry in the library: it is the process that produced every other project skill here, and it was requested at least eight separate times. It compounds — each use makes the next session cheaper.

maintenance.why: Almost entirely principle. The only vendor-specific part is the frontmatter shape.

failureModes.why: The multi-agent silent-zero trap is a genuinely non-obvious failure — a truncated fan-out returns confirmedCount 0, which reads as 'no bugs found' — and the recovery via journal.jsonl is specific and actionable.

reuseLeverage.why: Applies to every long build in this environment, and the user named the constraint himself as his main problem.

maintenance.why: Mostly durable practice; only the journal.jsonl recovery path is tied to a specific harness.

failureModes.why: Its core contribution is an explicit list of tools in this environment that return false results — the preview pane freezing rAF, vercel domains inspect misreporting ownership, env pull returning empty for sensitive vars, a local dev server sending no CSP — which is precisely the evidence a verification pass would otherwise trust.

reuseLeverage.why: Fires before every 'done', which is every task, and the pglite harness pattern is directly reusable on any Postgres-backed project.

maintenance.why: The discipline and the reporting format are durable; the specific list of lying tools is environment-bound and will need pruning.

failureModes.why: The strongest failure documentation in the library: four numbered builds, what each tried, why each failed, and the generalised diagnostic — 'nothing happens and no error either' means the page's JavaScript never executed, not that the key is wrong — plus three curl commands that isolate browser from code.

reuseLeverage.why: Applies to any internal or owner-facing panel, which is a recurring but not constant need.

maintenance.why: Forms, links and server rendering are the most stable things on the web; only the filesystem-before-rewrites note is vendor-specific.

failureModes.why: The fail-open guard is shown as wrong-code-then-right-code, and the 'do not count an admin login as presence' correction is a security property that is invisible until named — an attacker who got in would otherwise sustain their own lockout of the owner.

reuseLeverage.why: Needed on every product with an owner panel, and the inactivity-failover hierarchy is an unusual design most projects never think to build.

maintenance.why: HMAC cookies and timing-safe comparison are stable primitives; nothing here depends on a vendor's current behaviour.

failureModes.why: Names the default failure of every long-running agent — a knowledge base that only grows becomes confidently wrong — and the concrete ack-failure bug where a pre-parsed body caused every sync to silently re-run the same work.

reuseLeverage.why: The architecture transfers to any monitoring or growth agent, and the observed-not-self-reported training signal is the most portable idea in the whole repo.

maintenance.why: The patterns are platform-independent; only the specific fingerprinting examples and the OAuth/metric-naming notes are tied to current platform behaviour.

failureModes.why: Every entry is a trap that already cost hours on this machine, and the worst one — a .cmd shim truncating a multi-line prompt at the first newline so the model answers a question it never received — produces plausible output, which is why it survives for days undetected.

reuseLeverage.why: Fires on every script that shells out or gets scheduled on this workstation, which is the only workstation in play.

maintenance.why: PowerShell 5.1 and cmd.exe behaviour will not change; the specific credential and CLI paths will.

failureModes.why: Four distinct real failures with their diagnoses: the 403 that is a sender-domain validation error and not a bad key, the double unique index that turns a duplicate into a 500, the +tag regex that rejected every real Gmail alias, and the form that stored eight enquiries while notifying nobody for three weeks.

reuseLeverage.why: Every project here has a form, and the canonicalization plus unique-index rule is the kind of thing that is cheap to get right once and expensive to discover in production.

maintenance.why: Gmail's dot/plus semantics and Postgres conflict behaviour are stable; the provider-specific 403 wording is not.

failureModes.why: Documents four failures that all present as 'nothing happened': a rewrite silently dead behind a static file, a form falling through because rewrites merge rather than replace the query string, a deploy refused at the twelfth function, and env pull returning empty for a variable that is actually set.

reuseLeverage.why: Every project in this environment is on the same plan, so the router-consolidation pattern is directly reusable — it already took one project from sixteen functions to four with no URL changes.

maintenance.why: Entirely composed of one vendor's current free-tier limits and resolution order. Numbers like 12 and 4.5 MB are exactly the sort of thing that changes without warning.

failureModes.why: The money-safety rules are each stated as the failure they prevent, and the dead shared-sandbox credentials are called out with the verbatim 9999 error so nobody spends a day debugging their own code.

reuseLeverage.why: High value inside Bangladesh and zero outside it. The idempotency and server-side-pricing rules do generalise to any gateway.

maintenance.why: The API version path and the go-live process are bKash's to change, and the merchant portal has already changed once during this history.

failureModes.why: Two strong engineering rules drawn from the domain — never fire a rule on missing data, always state consequence and fix — plus the worked cascade example that a wrong implementation will visibly fail, but it is knowledge rather than an incident log.

reuseLeverage.why: This is the owner's actual expertise encoded, and it is the input every product here depends on. It is also the part an assistant cannot derive from a codebase.

maintenance.why: The tariff dataset is republished every fiscal year and the rates change with it; UCP 600 and the cascade structure are durable, the numbers are not.

failureModes.why: It is an evaluation method, so it documents how a review fails — flattery, hedging into uselessness, no falsification condition — rather than technical symptoms.

reuseLeverage.why: Already changed a product's whole strategy once by returning ~6/10 and killing the labour-savings pitch, and the user asks for this frame repeatedly and acts on the answer.

maintenance.why: Nothing version-bound. Only the market-reality numbers, like the $150-400/month merchandiser figure, will drift.

failureModes.why: Identifies the specific handoff failures — a step with no expected result so the owner cannot distinguish success from silence, an optional-looking variable that silently disables email, and a limitation discovered at the worst moment — but few technical symptoms.

reuseLeverage.why: The owner does not code, so every single deliverable in this environment ends in a handoff shaped by this skill.

maintenance.why: Pure communication practice; nothing here depends on a version or a vendor.

failureModes.why: Names the four places fabrication actually enters — design imports carrying confident placeholder copy, filling out a thin-looking section, re-deploys restoring an old file, and summaries dropping a hedge — and ships a grep gate that catches regression mechanically.

reuseLeverage.why: Applies to every page published under a real person's name, and the pre-deploy grep is a permanent mechanism rather than a reminder.

maintenance.why: The rules are absolute and timeless; only the specific corrected-facts list is project-bound, and it lives next to the facts it guards.

failureModes.why: Explains why DOM scraping returns nothing on lazy-loaded pages, why reconstructing title-to-id pairing from embedded JSON produces mismatches, that Facebook needs a retry before OG tags appear, and which URL shapes are signed and will die.

reuseLeverage.why: The general method — embedded state, then oEmbed, then crawler UA, then OG tags — transfers to most platforms, and it is what makes real content available instead of invented content.

maintenance.why: It depends on undocumented internals of two platforms. ytInitialData's shape and Facebook's crawler response are both things that change without notice, and the skill will silently rot rather than error.

failureModes.why: Covers the signed-CDN-URL trap that yields a broken image next week, the raqm-less Pillow that cannot shape Bengali with no runtime workaround, the immutable-cache trap, and the 256 KiB API cap that decodes to corrupt files.

reuseLeverage.why: The local-and-free-first default already replaced a paid generation once, and the imagery question recurs on every site build.

maintenance.why: ffmpeg and the caching rules are durable; the generation-tool landscape and the specific MCP notes turn over quickly.

failureModes.why: Its main contribution is naming the non-engineering failure modes — platform policy on mass-produced content, a single-account strike risk, and five free-tier services being five silent breakage points — which is what actually kills this class of project.

reuseLeverage.why: Single-purpose scoping document for one open request. Valuable precisely once, though the honesty template for pushing back on an unreachable target does generalise.

maintenance.why: Rests on current platform monetization policy and current API quota numbers, both of which move, and on an ask that has not been decided yet.
